newsitem.title: JAPAN: Minor Metals--Cobalt seen rebounding despite DLA.
newsitem.headline: Minor Metals--Cobalt seen rebounding despite DLA.

text.p: Cobalt prices are set for a rebound in the near future, despite news that the U.S. Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) is likely to resume sales of the metal from its stockpiles next month, traders said on Tuesday.

"The price is likely to rise in the short term," said a trader at one of Japan's major trading houses. "High-grade cobalt may move towards $25 (per pound), though fresh factors would be needed for prices to exceed that level."

Traders said cobalt prices, which had eased after Laurent Kabila took power in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, had started to firm already, helped by a four-week strike at the Sudbury plant of Canada's Inco Ltd.
High-grade cobalt was quoted at $22-23 per pound and low-grade cobalt at $18.75-20, they said.

A U.S. court ruling last week which lifted a restraining order on DLA cobalt stockpile sales did not weigh on upward momentum, particularly as many expected the DLA to reduce sales of the metal this fiscal year.

Dealers in New York said last week that the DLA was likely to offer 500,000 pounds of cobalt in August and another one million pounds in September, not even half of what the DLA is entitled to sell by the end of September.
The DLA has authority to sell six million pounds of cobalt in the current U.S. fiscal year ending in September, and has already sold about 2.1 million pounds.
Another cobalt trader in Tokyo said end-users' stocks were now running low, as the metal's price has stayed high so far this year.
Another bullish factor was the explosion over the weekend at the Harjavalta Metals Oy smelter of Finland's Outokumpu Oy, traders said.
In the magnesium market, spot prices for Chinese special high grade (SHG) were little changed at $2,350-2,600 per tonne.

"Demand from aluminium mills is likely to fall in the third quarter," said one magnesium trader. "Production for beverage cans has passed its peak. The window frame business is not faring well as housing demand is dropping quite a lot."

Traders said domestic prices for Chinese magnesium for deliveries in the third quarter rose by about $50 to $100 per tonne from the previous quarter, while prices for western magnesium climbed $200 to $250 per tonne.
The molybdenum spot market was quiet, with many players watching deliveries from U.S. Molycorp that started recently. It was quoted at $4.60-4.70 per pound.
"People want to wait a little as we've seen goods from Molycorp," said one trader.

Traders said prices of vandium, used in high-grade special steel, firmed ahead of the European summer, when many converters shut down. Ferro-vandium was quoted at $20 per kg, compared with $18.90 last week.
